 Judgment
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 17.05.2023.
2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 17.05.2023 at about 8.30 p.m., petitioner was standing on the left side of the road, carefully and cautiously by observing all traffic rules near A2B Hotel, Bhattarahalli O. M. Road, Bangalore, at that time KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No. KA-07-F-1740 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life, without following any traffic rules, at a high speed and dashed to the petitioner. Due to the forced impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body. Immediately, he was shifted to Sathya Sai Orthopaedic Hospital, wherein he treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, Conveyance, food, transport and other charges. 
The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 49 years, the petitioner doing Coolie work and earning a sum of Rs.1,000/- per day. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and lost his future income. Respondent being the owner cum internal insurer of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest. 
3. After service of notice, the respondent has appeared through his counsel and filed the written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition as false and contended that the petition is neither maintainable in law nor on facts and also denying the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle. He also denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner. This respondent further submitted that, the incident was occurred in night at 20.30 hours and the spot of the incident is National Highway road and there is no Zebra crossing at the spot of accident to cross the road by the pedestrian and since the petitioner has tried all of sudden to cross the High way road and came infront of bus, the accident in question has occurred and there is no rash and negligent act of the driver of the bus. Moreover, the petitioner in collusion with certain authorities has filed this false claim petitioner. By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. 
4. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor framed the following issues are as under:

2 1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 17.05.2023 at about 8.30 p.m., when he was standing in the left side of the road, carefully and cautiously by observing all the traffic near A2B hotel, Bhattarahalli O. M. Road, Bangalore, at that time, one KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No. KA-07-F- 1740 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life, came at high speed and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident and due to the forced impact,
petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries as alleged by him?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or Award?
5. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.14 and he has examined Dr. Nagaraj. B. N as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.15 and Ex.P.16 and closed their side. On the other hand, the driver of the offending KSRTC bus is examined as RW.1.
6. Heard arguments of both the sides and perused the materials placed on record. 
7. My findings on the above issues are as under; Issue No.1: In the affirmative. 
Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following:
:REASONS: 
8. ISSUE No.1: The petitioner has contended that on the above said date, time and place he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
9. The petitioner who is injured in this accident has got examined himself as PW-1 by reiterating the averments made in the petition. He has produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to 14. Ex.P.1 is the FIR,
Ex.P2 is the complaint, Ex.P.3 is the Charge-sheet, Ex.P.4 is the Hospital Intimation, Ex.P.5 is the Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.6 is the Sketch, Ex.P.7 is the Wound Certificate, Ex.P.8 is the IMV Report,
Ex.P.9 is the notice U/s 133 of the MV Act, Ex.P.10 is the Reply notice, Ex.P11 is the discharge summary, Ex.P12 is the Medical bills, Ex.P13 is the Medical Prescriptions, Ex.P14 is the Notarized copy of Voter Identity Card. 
10. On going through the materials, it could be seen that on on 17.05.2023 at about 8.30 p.m.,
petitioner was standing on the left side of the road, carefully and cautiously by observing all traffic rules near A2B Hotel, Bhattarahalli O. M. Road, Bangalore, at that time KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. 
No. KA-07-F-1740 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life,
Chowdappa Alias Chavdappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 29 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74446716/
3 without following any traffic rules, at a high speed and dashed to the petitioner. Due to the forced impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body. Immediately,
he was shifted to Sathya Sai Orthopaedic Hospital, wherein he treated as inpatient. Accordingly, the K. R. Puram Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.141/2023. After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
11. The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person. It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others. In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act. 
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something. In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do. The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent driving by the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg. No. KA-07-F-1740.
12. As we know evidence in any Summary Proceedings, " The act of Negligence" will have to be assessed on the basis of broad preponderance of probabilities and degree of proof required is not one of beyond reasonable doubt, as it is insisted in criminal case for " The Negligent Act ". 
13. The certified copy of the First Information (First information statement/s complaint in common para-lace) lodged before the K. R. Puram Traffic Police has been marked as Ex.P2. On receiving the First Information, the Station House Officer chose to register a case in Crime No. 141/2023. The said certified copy of First Information Report (F.I.R.) is marked as Ex.P1.
14. During the Course of examination-in-chief, he got marked Ex.P1 to 10 are the only documents,
which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of driving by the driver of offending KSRTC Bus. The Ex.P.5 (spot panchanama) and Ex.P.6 (Spot Sketch), clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information, held investigation and filed the Ex.P.3, Charge-Sheet against the driver of the offending KSRTC Bus U/s. 279 and 338 of IPC. The Ex. P.8 i.e. , certified copy of the IMV Report discloses that, the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle in question. 
15. In order to rebut the claim of the petitioner, respondent examined the driver of the said KSRTC Bus with Token No.4763 as RW.1 and deposed that, while coming back from Tirupathi to Bangalore his bus at Bhatarahalli opposite A2B Hotel, passengers making noise stating that one pedestrian was fell down, immediately he stopped his bus wherein he found that, one person right leg got wounded saying that, KSRTC Bus caused the accident. With the help of local people and ambulance said person was taken to the hospital. But without his fault K. R. Puram Traffic Police filed false case against him. During the course of cross- examination he admits that, criminal case is pending against him in another court. So, by going through the above admission itself goes to show that, till today driver of the KSRTC Bus i.e., RW-1 has not challenged the charge-sheet filed against him. 
Admittedly, said case is still pending. 
Chowdappa Alias Chavdappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 29 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74446716/
4 16. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
17. In view of the detailed discussion held above, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner has proved negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle and as such the accident in question had taken place. By relying on evidence of P.W.1 and the Police records, I am of the considered view that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No. KA-07-F-1740. Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative. 
18. ISSUE No.2: The petitioner in his evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Sathya Sai Orthopaedic Hospital, Bangalore wherein he was admitted was inpatient and he took treatment. Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
19. PAIN AND SUFFERING: In the petition as well as in his evidence PW1 deposed that,
immediately after the accident he was shifted to Sathya Sai Orthopaedic Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient. The petitioner has produced the discharge card marked at Ex.P.11,
wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner was admitted in the Sathya Sai Orthopaedic & Multi- Specialty Hospital, Bangalore from 17.05.2023 to 20.05.2023 i.e., 03 days. He has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.7, wherein the doctor has opined that, petitioner has sustained Communited fracture of the lower end of the right tibia with dislocation of the 1st MTP and fracture of the metatarsal and the said injuries are grievous in nature. Hence, it is clear that during the above said period the petitioner suffered lot of pain and inconvenience. Considering all these aspects this tribunal has granted Rs.40,000/- under the head of pain and suffering. 
20. MEDICAL EXPENSES: The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses. In support of his plea, he has produced 20 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.12 to the tune of Rs.1,36,094/-. Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner. The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,36,094/-
towards medical expenses. 
21. LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID UP PERIOD: The petitioner has produced Ex.P.11 Discharge summary issued by Sathya Sai Orthopaedic & Multi-Specialty Hospital, Bangalore, it reveals that, the petitioner took treatment in the said hospital from 17.05.2023 to 20.05.2023 i.e.,
03 days. Hence, at least 1 months is required to recover from the accidental injuries. It is the further contention that, the injured petitioner was doing Coolie work and earning a sum of Rs.1,000/- per day, but no reliable evidence is produced by the petitioner. So, in the absence of any evidence in respect of the income of the petitioner, if he is consider as doing Coolie work in the year 2023, the petitioner might have monthly income at Rs.16,000/-. The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2023 at Rs.16,000/- per month for determination of income before Lok-Adalat for the Districts coming under the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru Bench. 
The accident is of the year is 2023. Hence, the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/-
p.m. as per above decision. Hence, 1 months is to be considered as loss of income. Hence, he is Chowdappa Alias Chavdappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 29 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74446716/
5 entitled for compensation of Rs.16,000/- under this head. 
22. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability- The petitioner to prove his disability, he has produced the evidence of Dr. Nagaraj. B. N as PW.2 in order to substantiate the same, PW.2 who has opined that, total physical disability of right lower limb at 47% and that of whole body disability at 16%. Admittedly, the PW.2 is not a treated doctor. 
Same was admitted by the PW.2 during his cross examination, the relevant evidence of the PW.2 reads as follows :
"It is true to say that I have not personally treated the petitioner." 
He was sworn that, petitioner has got 16% disability to the whole body but he was not issued the disability certificate. It is quite but natural that to help the petitioner doctor will give exaggerated disability. However, looking to the nature of the injuries it is proper to came to conclusion that there is 8% of disability to the petitioner. 
23. Before proceeding on merits of the claim the age of the petitioner /injured has to be determined. 
Ex.P.14 is the Voter Identity Card of the petitioner, wherein his D.O.B is mentioned as 01.01.1974 and accident took place in the year 2023. Accordingly, I assess his age as 49 years at the time of this accident. As per the ruling reported in AIR 2009 SCW page-3014 between SARLA VERAMA AND OTHERS VS DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND OTHERS, the relevant multiplier applicable is '13'. Hence Rs.16,000 X 12 X 13 X 8% = 1,99,680/-. Under this head the petitioner is entitled for an amount of Rs./-.
24. FOOD, CONVEYANCE, NOURISHMENT AND ATTENDANT CHARGES: 
Further the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took treatment as inpatient in Sathya Sai Orthopaedic & Multi-Specialty Hospital, Bangalore, as inpatient from 17.05.2023 to 20.05.2023 i.e., 03 days. Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of nutritious food and attendant charges. 
25. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS: The petitioner was aged about 49 years at the time of accident, he has sustained grievous injuries. It shows that he found difficulty in doing day to day works. He might have suffered lot of pain and loss of amenities and comforts in life. 
Therefore, considering the age, nature of injuries and percentage of disability, Rs.50,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and happiness. 
26. TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES : The petitioner has also claimed compensation towards future medical expenses. The doctor who has been examined as PW.2 has suggested for removal of the implants and estimate of this surgery will be approximately Rs.60,000/-. By keeping nature of the injuries sustained, as he is bound to suffer medical problems in future and cannot every time depend upon Government hospital. Hence, under this head Rs.40,000/- is awarded. 
Chowdappa Alias Chavdappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 29 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74446716/
6 Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
1 Pain and sufferings Rs. 40,000/-
2 Medical expenses Rs. 1,36,094/-
3 Loss of earnings during laid Rs. 16,000/-
up period 4 Loss of future earning, Rs. 1,99,680/-
Disability 5 Nutritious food and Rs. 30,000/-
attendant charges 6 Loss of future amenities and Rs. 50,000/-
happiness 7 Future Medical expenses Rs. 40,000/-
Total Rs. 5,11,774/-
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,11,774/- under various heads. 
27. LIABILITY: As discussed in issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing Reg. No. KA-07-F-1740 and the police have conducted due enquiry and filed charge sheet against the said driver of the KSRTC bus bearing Reg.
No. KA-07-F-1740. However, the respondent being the owner cum internal insurer of the offending KSRTC bus is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. 
28. INTEREST: As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%. By relying on the aforesaid decision,
6% interest awarded to the petitioners in the present case on hand. Accordingly, issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative. 
29. ISSUE No.3: In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
:ORDER:
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I.M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.5,11,774/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization. 
Chowdappa Alias Chavdappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 29 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74446716/
7 The respondents is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner with interest. The respondent being insurer is liable to deposit the amount before Tribunal within two months from the date of this order. 
In the event of deposit of total compensation amount of petitioner, 50% of amount shall be released in his favour along with interest thereon. 
 Remaining 50% of compensation amount of  petitioner in total compensation amount including interest thereon shall be deposited in his name as F.D. in any of the Nationalized or Scheduled Bank as per choice of petitioner for a period of two years. 
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.
2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated:19.08.2019. 
The petitioner is hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contains compulsorily photograph of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank. Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Adhar Card. 
In case of deposit of awarded amount, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal. 
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission by the Tribunal. 
Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner after expiry of two years period of deposit on proper verification and identification,
without waiting for further order of court. 
The advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-. 
Draw award accordingly.

Bengaluru.

Remaining 50% of compensation amount of  petitioner in total compensation amount including interest thereon shall be deposited in his name as F.D. in any of the Nationalized or Scheduled Bank as per choice of petitioner for a period of two years.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.
2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated:19.08.2019.

The petitioner is hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contains compulsorily photograph of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Adhar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission by the Tribunal.

Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner after expiry of two years period of deposit on proper verification and identification,
without waiting for further order of court.
The advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
